name: Warm-water bidet seat
summary: A toilet seat with a heater and a hidden nozzle that sprays warm water. A small pump and a water heater inside the seat replace a separate bidet.
how: Heat the seat to about 36 °C with an electric element.
Store a small volume of water and heat it to about 38 °C when needed.
Hide the nozzle in a cover and rinse it with clean water before and after each use.
Place the controls on the side of the seat or on a wall remote.

origin.note: Toto launches the Washlet, a toilet seat with a warm-water spray, for the Japanese home.

adoptions.via: A Japanese maker fits the seat on a plain vitreous china WC, and the seat carries the water, heat and control.
Designer ranges adopt the seat on a wall-hung bowl as an option.
